The Python patcher and C tester do not establish any additional host CPU target. Build: The root distributes patched PRG/CRT/D64 artifacts and tester source/binary. Source and payload were inspected without compiling the tester, executing the patcher or playing patched binaries. Limitations: All build flags stay unknown. notes: Identity: Greaseweazle Rescue is a substantive AutoIt Windows GUI and recovery-workflow layer over Greaseweazle. The current root contains v1.3.4 source and release notes, despite root README installation examples still naming v1.3.1. It handles PC/DOS/VGACopy, AmigaDOS ADF and C64/1541 D64 workflows. Classification: The source implements format detection, SCP capture, standard ADF/D64 conversion, direct retry reads, reports, hashes and conflict-safe publication of complete logical images. Its DOS path additionally implements targeted head-by-head adaptive rereads and multi-SCP sector merging. This is independent recovery automation around an existing decoder, rather than a claim to have reimplemented Greaseweazle's flux codecs. Limitations: The multi-SCP handler explicitly rejects Amiga and C64 modes. Advanced adaptive two-pass sector recovery is DOS-only; Amiga/C64 use direct Greaseweazle retry reads. Complete ADF/D64 standard sectors do not preserve all copy-protection or unusual flux data, so SCP remains the archival master. Source CPU: This tool reads floppy flux and disk-image sector data rather than reconstructing any original executable CPU instruction set. Supported disk platforms do not establish source CPUs. The loader creates PSP/environment and synthetic interrupt stubs; DOS file calls use native host fopen/fread/fwrite and -r maps a host directory to C:. Original executables run without a booted DOS OS or vendor ROM in the normal path. Optional boot-sector loading does not establish a complete PC hardware emulator. status: Primary source reviewed; independent build/run not performed
notes:

Actual implementation locates tracks, identifies WAVE/BINARY formats, sorts by track number, formats pregaps and writes the cue file. Classification: Small but complete implementation, not a placeholder. notes: TRS-80/TCS Genie IIIs emulator derived from SDL2TRS/xtrs with independently implemented OMTI, WD1000/1010 and Xebec S1410 hard-disk paths. title: Starflight Reverse
notes: Reverse engineering of the 1986 DOS game Starflight. The project exploits retained/encrypted Forth word names and the game's indirect-threaded representation to recover thousands of words, decode overlays and emit C representations of the recovered routines. title: Vertigo
status: Original development discs and beebasm conversions; variant-specific recovery caveats
notes: Identity: The author identifies the archive as the complete source collection for Superior Software’s 1991 BBC Micro/Electron game and credits Richard Hanson’s permission to release it. Recovered development discs and converted source variants are documented separately. Classification: Original ADE+ sources were recovered and converted to beebasm syntax. This is source restoration and reproducible-build research, not a binary-derived disassembly. Source includes the main game handler, enemy paths, levels, lives and scoring. Source CPU: The BBC Master main source explicitly selects CPU 1 (65C02), and the handler uses STZ/DEA. BBC B and Electron variants use conventional 6502 instructions and platform-specific source sets. Both precise ISA values are retained instead of collapsing every variant to 6502. Target CPU: The four Makefile targets assemble the preserved Master, BBC B disc, BBC B cassette and Electron cassette variants. Their output instruction sets remain 65C02 for the inspected Master path and 6502 for the BBC B/Electron paths; the modern beebasm build host is not a target CPU. Build: Makefile clones/builds beebasm and assembles four SSD outputs. The author reports a byte match for the older Master backup, whose title art says 1989 rather than the final 1991 release. BBC B disc recovery was corrupted; the cassette source appears incomplete, and Electron relocation/data mismatches required fixes. These are variant-specific author reports, not our verified results. Limitations: No assembler build, launch, gameplay, cassette conversion or byte comparison was performed. evidence: Explicit Claude co-author trailer and Claude Code session reference in commit 0a68fabbad5e4c4572fcd91066f050250da3f1b3: https://github.com/sidick/volamos/commit/0a68fabbad5e4c4572fcd91066f050250da3f1b3
Claude co-author trailer observed in recent tracked commits: 1 in this scan (example 53ad8f07e2cf; Claude)

notes: Wine-style host runtime for classic AmigaOS m68k command-line tools: interprets guest instructions (optional m68k-crate trace JIT) and reimplements OS library calls in Rust. No Kickstart ROM is needed for normal use. It is generic development/analysis tooling, not a native reconstruction of a specific game; graphics, custom chips, Workbench GUI and games are explicitly out of scope. Linux/macOS build and guest execution are corroborated by current CI logs; published Windows x86-64 binaries compile but Windows/Wine runtime remains unverified. Interpreter/JIT parity covers six fixtures; comparison with vamos includes three documented known divergences, so it is not universal compatibility proof. The math-library shims now return comparison/test results in both D0 and 68k condition codes, matching the documented ROM calling behavior needed by SAS/C's scmieee.lib; before the fix, SAS/C double comparisons appeared equal and exp() overflow checks returned HUGE_VAL. Evidence: https://github.com/sidick/volamos/commit/de321627fd5f1c16ca6cc76020222d7f3c18d564 exec.library SetFunction now installs executable guest JMP entries, returns a synthesized callable stub for the previous host-backed handler, supports hook chaining and restoration, and is covered by an end-to-end guest test. The patch is deliberately limited to one guest invocation and does not emulate AmigaOS-wide persistent hooks. Evidence: https://github.com/sidick/volamos/commit/018fd8f047d27fa3f85948b1595f44acf3f6f596 v0.10 incorporates non-AUTOINIT disk-library loading and the MakeLibrary/AddLibrary/InitStruct/MakeFunctions exec paths. Current main also adds opt-in CLI handling for UAE's formatted debug port at $BFFF00 and Emu68's byte debug port at $DEADBEEF, routing guest diagnostics to stderr without claiming broader GUI/custom-chip emulation. Evidence: https://github.com/sidick/volamos/releases/tag/v0.10 https://github.com/sidick/volamos/commit/2ee28f5f2759a9ea5096ba7f0068c4ec4cf94011 https://github.com/sidick/volamos/commit/359f762476c061b3b487cdcaf1dc86acdc786dd9 https://github.com/sidick/volamos/commit/fcec136d6f7f416b89af11d6bb76f6c89c96a8f5
